text: Now, the topic menu on the contact form. Back to our contact form. We add a topic menu that starts on delivery. In ContactForm.jsx, line four is our name state, starting as an empty string. Line five is the new one, topic with setTopic, starting as delivery, so the menu starts on delivery. And line six is the message state, also starting empty. The menu sits between the name box and the message box. It's a label with the word topic and inside it a select tag. Its value is topic in curly braces, and its onChange calls setTopic with e.target.value. That value must match the value of one option. And there are three option tags: Delivery, Payment, and Other, which the user reads as delivery, payment, and other. The user types Anna and picks Payment. Topic now holds payment, and the menu shows Payment. Figure twenty-one has the whole form. The heading Contact Us, the name box with Anna in it, the topic menu reading Payment, then an empty message box with a counter that says zero of two hundred, and the Send button at the bottom. Now, a slip that catches a lot of people. Reading e.target.value on the tick box. Next, we add the tick box, Email me a reply. Line seven of ContactForm.jsx gives it a state, wantsReply with setWantsReply, and it starts as false. Now, the developer copies the handler from the text boxes. So the input with type equals checkbox gets checked equals wantsReply in curly braces, which is fine. But its onChange calls setWantsReply with e.target.value. That line is marked wrong. It reads a fixed string, not the tick, and under it come the words, "Email me a reply." The user ticks the box and it looks ticked. Then the user clicks again to untick it, and it stays ticked. In figure twenty-two, the form still shows Anna and Payment. But now there's a tick next to Email me a reply, and that tick is there even after the second click. The tick box has a value too, so why is reading it wrong? Here is what happens. The user ticks the box and React calls onChange. On a tick box, e.target.value is a fixed string that never changes with the tick. When the tick box has no value of its own, the browser makes this string on. So setWantsReply saves the string on. React treats any text that is not empty as ticked, so the box is ticked. So far so good. Then the user clicks again to untick. The browser removes the tick for a moment, and React calls onChange again. But e.target.value is still on, so state is still on. [sighs] State did not change, so React puts the tick back and the box stays ticked. The fix is to read the tick itself. Same input, same checked equals wantsReply, only the onChange is different. It now calls setWantsReply with e.target.checked. That's true or false right after the click. After a reload, the box ticks and unticks with each click. And last in this section, send puts the menu and the tick box back. The send handler now puts every part of the form back to its start. Line fifteen opens handleSend, which takes e, and line sixteen calls e.preventDefault. Line seventeen logs sent, followed by name, topic, message, and wantsReply. Then the resets. Line eighteen empties the name. Line nineteen sets topic back to delivery, the first option. Line twenty empties the message, and line twenty-one sets wantsReply back to false, so the box is unticked again. Notice that no line of our code touches the menu or the tick box. So why does send put topic back to delivery and untick the box? The steps are the same as for the text box. The send handler saves delivery in topic and false in wantsReply. React renders ContactForm again, and React writes delivery into the menu and false into the tick box. Let's pull principle four together. Menus and tick boxes, the same pair with their own props. Control a menu with value on the select itself. Never selected on an option. Control a tick box with checked and read e.target.checked in its handler. A menu reports the value of the picked option, so value on the select must match one option. Writing selected on an option is the plain HTML habit, and React does not support it. A tick box holds true or false, so it takes checked from state. Its e.target.value is a fixed string, such as on, which never changes with the tick. So do this. Put value equals topic in curly braces on the select tag with setTopic reading e.target.value. The choice lives on the select. And give the tick box checked equals wantsReply with setWantsReply reading e.target.checked. Don't do this. Don't write selected on the payment option because React does not support it. And don't let the tick box handler read e.target.value. It's always on, so the box never unticks.
